rubric_additions.rubric-13:
Rule: Use the exporter list exactly as the installed Java SDK parses it.
Example: If the installed SDK accepts an exporter list containing both otlp and console, local-log isolation must preserve console.
Evidence: Accepted surrounding whitespace and mixed lists containing otlp must still receive local-receiver approval and header checks. When isolating an added OTLP member, preserve the remaining non-OTLP exporters. Do not turn SDK-invalid duplicate names or none mixed with other exporters into successful startup. Determine normalization and supported combinations from the installed SDK owner; do not replace its parser or test unused combinations.
Insufficient evidence: A custom list parser or a conflict path that silently converts SDK-invalid selection into successful startup.
rubric_additions.rubric-14:
Rule: A synthetic Java LoggingEvent or appender probe is focused SDK/bridge evidence even when a javaagent is attached.
Example: A test constructs a synthetic LoggingEvent while the Java agent is attached. It still proves the synthetic appender path, not a real application call site.
Evidence: Starting the agent does not make that synthetic probe app_test or full_runtime.
Insufficient evidence: Agent startup alone used to classify a synthetic event as app_test or full_runtime.
rubric_additions.rubric-15:
Rule: When adding a Java identity fallback, test SDK-accepted whitespace around Resource entries through the normal launcher.
Example: A shell check that recognizes only service.name=value can miss an SDK-accepted entry with surrounding spaces and append an overriding duplicate.
Evidence: Compact-only inputs would miss that failure. Preserve supplied configuration and SDK parsing; do not introduce a shell Resource parser.
Insufficient evidence: Compact-only Resource inputs or a replacement shell parser used to claim preservation through the real launcher.
rubric_additions.rubric-23:
Rule: Prove Java appender value support using the resolved dependency and actual bridge path.
Example: An array accepted by a direct typed SDK emit can still be unsupported by the resolved appender bridge.
Evidence: Mapper code from upstream main, another release, or a direct typed-SDK empty-array test does not prove the appender preserves that value. Report an observed limitation of a selected value without forcing a fixed release or replacing the provider. Ordinary absence of an optional value remains valid.
Insufficient evidence: A direct-SDK or upstream-main mapper test used as proof of the installed appender path.
rubric_additions.rubric-25:
Rule: If the Java requirements select repeated keep-alive requests or executor/thread reuse, retain assertions for those actual repeated rounds and the same reused execution unit.
Example: One left/right request pair cannot establish selected executor reuse across repeated rounds.
Evidence: One concurrent left/right pair does not prove them; missing evidence remains unproven. The fixture uses CompletableFuture.runAsync. Audit plans to verify propagation provided by the selected Java agent/runtime. Instrumentation reuses that integration when it already works instead of adding redundant manual context copying. Verification checks the current real request-to-async join without editing code. A standalone/manual SDK mode needs its own supported context-handoff evidence.
Insufficient evidence: One successful pair, or a language-wide assumption, in place of the selected repeated-round and same-unit assertions.
rubric_additions.rubric-27:
Rule: For captured Spring MVC error or argument diagnostics, find a supported hook on the actual producer path.
Example: A Tomcat JULI diagnostic may bypass a Spring MVC error handler and render throwable data later. Inspect the actual supported producer hook.
Evidence: A sufficient logging-only repair need not change controllers or investigate every alternative. Inspect Tomcat JULI/JUL producers that can bypass MVC handlers, including the installed LogRecord, Filter, Handler and bridge APIs, whether the filter runs, and how parameters or throwables are rendered. Do not mutate records after asynchronous handoff, change global logger levels per request, or replace operator handlers. Audit plans the investigation. Instrumentation repairs and replays a supported selected path. Verification reports the boundary actually checked without unauthorized application edits.
Insufficient evidence: An MVC-only filter used to claim that a different container producer was sanitized.
rubric_additions.rubric-28:
Rule: For the selected Java malformed-request diagnostic, preserve the response status, headers and body, and the diagnostic category.
Example: If the failing request returns a specific error response, replay that same request after sanitization and compare the response and diagnostic category.
Evidence: Replay that same malformed request and check that later rendering does not log the raw value or stack. A different successful request cannot prove this preservation.
Insufficient evidence: A successful request used to prove preservation of the malformed-request response or absence of later raw rendering.
rubric_additions.rubric-58:
Rule: When a known local-log conflict can safely be isolated in the selected JVM startup path, disable only the added local-log branch.
Example: A known safely isolated log-header conflict disables the added OTLP log branch while the application, native logs, traces and metrics still start.
Evidence: Preserve application startup, native logging, traces, metrics and the original operator headers. Unresolved ownership of JVM arguments remains an explicit preflight blocker. Plan or run the selected normalized-OTLP conflict and the approved signal-specific endpoint A with unused generic endpoint B through the actual launcher.
Insufficient evidence: An environment-only check without the selected actual launcher case, or ignoring unresolved JVM-argument ownership.
